s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute tender nodule on the forehead with granulomatous inflammation and yeast infection
salient_findings: Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
Granulomatous inflammation with numerous narrow-budding yeasts
key_facts: Presented with a tender nodule on her forehead
History of bumping her forehead on an air-conditioning unit several months prior
Denied fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia
Lived alone with a pet cat and spent minimal time outdoors
No recent exposure to systemic steroids
Skin biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with numerous narrow-budding yeasts

raw.syndrome_frame: Subacute tender nodule on the forehead with granulomatous inflammation and yeast infection
salient_findings: Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
Granulomatous inflammation with numerous narrow-budding yeasts
key_facts: Presented with a tender nodule on her forehead
History of bumping her forehead on an air-conditioning unit several months prior
Denied fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia
Lived alone with a pet cat and spent minimal time outdoors
No recent exposure to systemic steroids
Skin biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with numerous narrow-budding yeasts

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with numerous narrow-budding yeasts and tissue culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans

shortlist.label: Sporotrichosis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute tender nodule on the forehead with granulomatous inflammation, consistent with sporotrichosis, although less likely than cryptococcosis

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and yeast infection, although histoplasmosis is less likely given the lack of exposure history and negative laboratory tests

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to blastomycosis, but less likely given the skin biopsy and tissue culture results

shortlist.label: Chromoblastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and yeast infection, although chromoblastomycosis is less likely given the clinical presentation and lack of characteristic sclerotic bodies

raw.rationale: The skin biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules, and tissue culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans, which is consistent with Cryptococcosis. The patient's immunocompromised state due to fingolimod treatment for multiple sclerosis also increases the risk of Cryptococcosis.

rejected.label: Sporotrichosis
rejected.why: Sporotrichosis typically presents with a lymphocutaneous pattern and is more commonly associated with outdoor activities and trauma, which is not consistent with the patient's minimal outdoor exposure.

rejected.label: Histoplasmosis
rejected.why: Histoplasmosis is more commonly associated with pulmonary symptoms and would likely have shown positive results on chest radiography or blood cultures, which were negative in this case.

rejected.label: Blastomycosis
rejected.why: Blastomycosis typically presents with more severe symptoms, including fever and respiratory issues, which the patient denied, and the skin biopsy findings do not match the typical broad-based budding yeasts seen in Blastomycosis.

rejected.label: Chromoblastomycosis
rejected.why: Chromoblastomycosis is a chronic fungal infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue, typically presenting with long-standing lesions and is more common in tropical regions, which does not fit the patient's presentation or history.
